[RDSC.7.6] The complete atom registry.

An atom's identity on the wire is its `oneof` field number ([RFCS.16.1]), and
its name is its body message: the `Atom` column below, which is also how
[RDSC.8.1]'s grammar states it as a terminal. **That number is the `Field #`
column**, which is the field the atom occupies in `proto/atom.proto#Atom`'s
`body` oneof — so a reader holding [RDSC.7.1] and not the proto can identify an
atom and not merely frame one. A struck row is out of use: its `Field #`
cell names the numbers `proto/atom.proto#Atom` reserves for it, and they are
never reissued.

The test atoms (`TestCase` / `TestFact` / `TestCacheSeed` / `TestResponse` /
`TestReply`) and the oracle atoms (`OracleActivated` / `OracleEmit` /
`OraclePublish` / `OracleCall` / `OracleCacheSet` / `OracleCacheDelete` /
`OracleLog` / `OracleRetract` / `OracleWorkingMemory` / `OracleExclusive`) are
test metadata ([LTSL] / [RTIM]): a production runtime's loader skips them
([RDSC.9.4]) and runs reactive execution unchanged. Each holds a field number of its own, so a self-contained
`[DSC][StreamHeader]` stream ([RFCS.13]) stays unambiguous ([RDSC.7.5]). A
bundle carrying them costs a non-test runtime only file size.
